analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily (2026-11-06)
key_insights: Yesterday's tech rout became the dominant cross-asset story. The Nasdaq Composite fell around 5.5% and the sell-off spread beyond AI names, in what Mizuho describes as looking like a positioning flush. The midterm relief rally did not last.
USTs bull-steepened sharply. 2Y yields tested 4.45% and 10Y yields approached 4.80%, more than 50bp below the October peak. The DXY rebounded to around 101.90.
Markets are starting to price greater political resistance to the AI and data-centre buildout after the Democratic sweep. The sell-off was most acute in semiconductors and data-centre-linked names.

Asian tech followed Wall Street lower overnight. Mizuho expects equities to remain the immediate directional input for duration today. If yesterday proves capitulatory and risk stabilises, some of the safe-haven bid could come out of USTs.

Oil is a second driver. Post-election hopes of de-escalation with Iran pushed Brent sharply below $100 earlier this week, but talks remain uncertain and Trump has said a decision may come soon. Brent tested $100 again overnight, so duration is vulnerable to renewed escalation.

Today's NFP is expected at about +65-70k with unemployment at 4.2%, which should keep the Fed focused on inflation. After this week's sharp repricing of hikes, a material downside surprise would reinforce the front-end rally. A modest beat would need stabilising equities and firmer oil alongside it to drive a meaningful reversal.

EGBs followed USTs, but the cross-market story was the OAT-Bund spread. It tightened towards 145bp on lower oil and a good French auction, then widened back towards 154bp after the US equity rout. The BTP-Bund move was similar. EUR/USD stayed under pressure around 1.1180.

For EGBs, another leg lower in risk assets should keep Bunds supported but is unlikely to help peripheral spreads after the recent OAT tightening. Equities stabilising with oil below $100 could reopen room for OAT and BTP tightening. Lane speaks at the ECB money market conference, but equities and oil matter more than the EUR calendar.

The BoE raised rates 25bp to 4%, as expected, but the 8-1 vote was not. Every member backed a hike and Mann preferred 50bp. Forecasts showed stronger activity, lower unemployment and materially higher inflation, with the conditioning curve already near 4.9% by end-2027.

Mizuho calls a December BoE hike live but still leans towards the MPC waiting for more data, given this week's drop in energy prices. Oil well above $100 would support hawkish pricing, while contained energy and soured risk sentiment could make the market question how quickly the MPC can follow up. Pill speaks this afternoon. One more hike looks hard to dismiss, with the debate over December versus 2027.
GBP/USD came under renewed downside pressure overnight, trading around 1.3410.
In Asia, risk weakness continued with tech leading. JGB 2-10Y yields fell by 10bp+ despite strong wage data. USD/JPY stayed near, but slightly below, 158 after testing sub-157.50.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Mizuho expects the print to keep the Fed focused on inflation. A material downside surprise would reinforce the front-end rally, while a modest beat needs stabilising equities and firmer oil to drive a reversal.
Paired with the payrolls forecast, it supports a Fed still focused on inflation rather than labour weakness.
The 25bp hike was expected. The 8-1 vote, with every member backing a hike and Mann preferring 50bp, was hawkish enough to make a December hike live.
Higher inflation forecasts came despite a market curve already pricing rates near 4.9%, which supports the hawkish read.
Oil fell sharply below $100 on de-escalation hopes with Iran earlier this week and tested $100 again overnight. It is a swing factor for duration and for UK rate expectations.

risk_factors: Renewed escalation with Iran pushing Brent well above $100, which would hurt duration and support hawkish BoE pricing.
A further leg lower in risk assets, which keeps Bunds supported but is unfriendly to peripheral spreads.
NFP surprise: a material downside miss would extend the front-end rally, while a beat needs equity and oil support to reverse it.
Political resistance to the AI and data-centre buildout after the Democratic sweep, hitting semiconductors and data-centre-linked names.
vol_and_positioning: Mizuho describes yesterday's tech sell-off, with the Nasdaq Composite down around 5.5%, as looking like a positioning flush. The open question is whether it was capitulatory enough to stabilise risk.
geopolitical: US-Iran negotiations remain uncertain. Trump's recent comments suggest a decision may come soon, and a renewed escalation would push oil above $100 and hurt duration.
The Democratic midterm sweep is read by markets as raising political resistance to the AI and data-centre buildout.
